manifest.name: Flood-Net private archive
manifest.tagline: Holds Flood-Net's historical site-inspection archive, which carries site access codes and must never be public.
manifest.about: A private repository beside Flood-Net. It keeps the historical inspection workbook and everything derived from it, because those carry site-access notes and codes meant only for the people who maintain the sites. Its own workflow runs Flood-Net's ingest tools against the archive on every push and daily. It is also where Flood-Net's weekly security review files its findings and keeps its log, so a hole is never published before it is fixed. Described here only from what Flood-Net says about it in public.

status.summary: Live: holds the archive and the security-review findings; Flood-Net's git history still holds the old archive until the owner runs the rewrite.
next: Run the history rewrite to scrub the archive from Flood-Net (cdomotor-g/MegaNet#239)

blocked.what: The rewrite needs the owner's computer: force-push, branch deletion, a GitHub Support purge

manifest.name: FW-LAB Receiver
manifest.tagline: An RTL-SDR and GNU Radio ALERT receiver with MQTT output, a web UI with live audio and waterfall, and forensics tools.
manifest.about: The Flood Warning ALERT Base Station Receiver: a GNU Radio flowgraph that demodulates and decodes ALERT1 bursts from an RTL-SDR, logs them as CSV and JSONL, and publishes them over MQTT. A Python web UI shows events, RF health, trends, path analysis and forensics, and scripts and systemd units run it unattended on a Pi with a cloud control plane. It came before Flood-Net: Flood-Net has taken its floodwarning.net domain and has a runbook to retire it, and RPi ALERT now does its base-station job.

status.summary: Dormant since about May 2026 and being retired: Flood-Net took floodwarning.net from it, and RPi ALERT replaced it as the base-station receiver.
next: Copy, then archive the repository with a README line pointing to Flood-Net

manifest.name: Quansheng ALERT receiver (UV-K5, archived)
manifest.tagline: The first ALERT receiver firmware, for the older DP32G030 Quansheng UV-K5 family. Archived; still builds and flashes.
manifest.about: Firmware for the UV-K5, UV-K5(8) and UV-K6 (DP32G030, bootloader 2.x), built on egzumer's firmware, that turns the handheld into an ALERT flood-telemetry receiver with a station table generated from Flood-Net. It was archived when work moved to the UV-K5 V3, but its builds and its own web installer still work, and in October 2026 it took the V3's on-air-proven demodulator and decoder. It needs a one-capacitor mod to hear the audio, and no modded radio has decoded on air yet.

status.summary: Archived and read-only; its last builds (20 October) carry the V3's decoder, but no modded UV-K5 has been tried on air yet.

manifest.name: F-TIDE
manifest.tagline: A decision-tree tool for assessing flood warning towers: guided questions, a delivery risk score and an exportable report.
manifest.about: Published as FWIN-ONSM-Matrix. Load a decision tree (tree.json), answer its questions about a tower, and export a self-contained HTML report with the path taken, the outcome and a Delivery Risk Score. The tree is edited in the browser (guided editor, a Cytoscape tree map, branches) and saved with a SHA-256-hashed changelog; a station register CSV the user loads fills in each site's details. It serves the same network's sites as Flood-Net but shares no code or data with it; Flood-Net neither absorbed nor replaced it.

status.summary: Working and published; the rule set (v57.2) was last edited in June 2026 and the app last built in July, with nothing since but a CLAUDE.md note.

manifest.name: ALERT_PACKETS
manifest.tagline: A one-page decoder and encoder for ALERT/ERTS packets (ABF, BCC, EAF, EIF), built on the Bureau's ERTS Data Formats spec.
manifest.about: Paste a 40-bit framed message, a 32-bit payload or 8-digit hex and it is decoded against every known format, with check bits and CRC validated and a colour-coded bit map; or encode the other way. Decoded addresses are named from a national ALERT address file, and the page can be driven from the URL with a JSON result. Flood-Net absorbed it: its ALERT Packets tab (packets.js) is the maintained port, carrying the same address file and spec byte for byte.

status.summary: Works as published but superseded by Flood-Net's ALERT Packets tab; last touched 13 Oct 2026, for a CLAUDE.md note only.
next: Point the README at Flood-Net's ALERT Packets tab as the maintained version

manifest.name: HTML-serial
manifest.tagline: A one-page Web Serial console: open a COM port in Chrome or Edge, set baud, bits, parity and flow control, and watch what arrives.
manifest.about: SerialTest.html, a single self-contained page that connects to a serial port through the browser's Web Serial API and prints what comes in. There is no README beyond the title and no published site. Flood-Net's Serial Monitor tab does the same job with the same port settings and much more (several ports, hex and ALERT decode, Quansheng, ERT-A2 and RTL-SDR cards, posting to Flood-Net), so it has replaced this in practice, though nothing in Flood-Net cites it.

status.summary: A dormant prototype, replaced by Flood-Net's Serial Monitor tab; not marked archived on GitHub, last touched 13 Oct 2026 for a CLAUDE.md note.

manifest.name: Home
manifest.tagline: A zero-cost smart-home dashboard: LPUs post sensor readings to ThingSpeak, and a GitHub Pages page charts them against the forecast.
manifest.about: A personal monitoring stack built around LPUs (Local Processing Units): field devices that each carry a few sensors and post to their own ThingSpeak channel over HTTPS. The first is a Campbell CR310 logging two rainwater tanks and a rain gauge; a Raspberry Pi with an RTL-SDR (rtl_433, for a 433 MHz weather station), a Pi camera and an ESP32 mushroom house are planned. It borrows the flood network's habits (Campbell loggers called LPUs, a Pi with an RTL-SDR) but shares no code or data with Flood-Net, which neither absorbed nor replaced it.
